items.title: Budget amendment: move reserves to road and sidewalk repair
items.summary: Moves $18 million from reserves to road and sidewalk repair. The staff summary is linked from the item page.
items.stakes: Anyone who depends on road and sidewalk repair: $18 million moves out of reserves for those repairs, so reserves shrink by that amount.
items.accountable: City Council voted on the budget amendment. The Finance department carries out the transfer.

items.title: Short-term rental permit enforcement update
items.summary: Informational report on complaints, inspections, and permit revocations citywide.
items.stakes: Neighbors of short-term rentals: the report summarizes complaints and permit actions and does not change any rule.
items.accountable: City Council received this report. Code enforcement and police handle the complaints.

items.title: Winter shelter capacity contract, 2026-27 season
items.summary: Adds 600 winter shelter beds across county-contracted sites.
items.stakes: People without shelter this winter: 600 winter beds would be added at county-contracted sites.
items.accountable: Board of Supervisors approved the contract. County health and housing staff manage the shelters.

items.title: Regional parks and trails maintenance report
items.summary: Annual maintenance backlog report with a list of trails scheduled for repair.
items.stakes: People who use county trails: the report lists which trails are scheduled for repair.
items.accountable: Board of Supervisors received this report. County parks staff schedule the repairs.

items.title: Park Boulevard corridor plan: presentation
items.summary: City staff presents the corridor plan for bike lanes, crossings, and parking changes, and asks for comments.
items.stakes: Cyclists, drivers, and businesses on Park Boulevard: the plan would change bike lanes, crossings, and parking.
items.accountable: Park Boulevard planning group recommends. The City Planning department prepares the plan, and City Council makes the final decision.

items.title: Short-term rental complaints report
items.summary: Code enforcement report on complaints in the planning area over the last quarter.
items.stakes: Neighbors of short-term rentals: the report shows complaint volume in the planning area.
items.accountable: Code enforcement presents the report. The planning group reviews it.

items.title: Officer elections
items.summary: Election of chair and vice chair for the coming year.
items.stakes: Planning group members: the election picks who leads and speaks for the group next year.
items.accountable: Planning group members elect their own chair and vice chair.

items.title: Council public comment rules (continued from Nov 16)
items.summary: Second reading of the speaking time rules. Staff proposes two minutes for general comment and three minutes for scheduled items.
items.stakes: Everyone who wants to speak at council meetings: if the rule passes, the new time limits apply at future meetings.
items.accountable: City Council votes on its own public comment rules.

items.title: Traffic calming, 30th Street between Upas and University
items.summary: Approves the design and $1.1 million for speed humps, a crossing signal, and a pilot bike lane.
items.stakes: Drivers, people walking, and bike riders on 30th Street: humps, a crossing signal, and a pilot bike lane would be built.
items.accountable: City Council approves the design and funding. Transportation staff carry out the work.

items.title: Outreach funding for recognized community planning groups
items.summary: Proposes annual outreach funding for recognized planning groups, including translation support.
items.stakes: Community planning groups and their neighbors: the funding would pay for notices and translation for outreach.
items.accountable: City Council votes on the funding. Recognized planning groups receive and spend it.

items.title: Six-month transit fare pilot on County routes
items.summary: Proposes reduced fares for youth and seniors on county-operated routes for six months.
items.stakes: Youth and seniors who ride county routes: fares would drop for six months if the pilot passes.
items.accountable: Board of Supervisors votes on the pilot. County transit staff run the routes.

items.title: Emergency medical services contract renewal
items.summary: Renews the ambulance services contract for three years with a new response-time standard.
items.stakes: Anyone who calls for an ambulance: the contract sets a new response-time standard for three years.
items.accountable: Board of Supervisors votes on the contract. County emergency services staff monitor response times.
